daysW5.title: Mansilla de las Mulas -> León
daysW5.short_desc: From a boring breakfast to a boutique Hotel in León
daysW5.long_desc: We started the day with a rather mediocre breakfast before leaving Mansilla de las Mulas, a town that, honestly, didn’t leave much of an impression. The albergue we stayed in was probably the best-maintained building in town, and our room was perfectly fine. However, no dinner or breakfast was served there, and we were directed to a nearby restaurant instead. After walking about 6 kilometers, we reached a small village where we treated ourselves to a second breakfast, this one far better and more energizing. The path into central León was long and fairly dull, following straight roads with little variety. But once we entered the city, the energy changed with beautiful architecture, lively streets, and the buzz of urban life were a welcome shift.We checked into My Palace León, a fantastic boutique hotel just a short walk from the city center. Comfortable rooms, great location, and a delicious breakfast made it feel like a well-earned reward. We’ll be staying here for two nights, and it feels great to finally pause and enjoy some comfort after nearly a month on the Camino.

daysW5.title: León - Rest day
daysW5.short_desc: Back pain, Podcast recording, and Pasta on the Plaza Regla in León
daysW5.long_desc: The day started a bit differently, Roy needed to have his back checked, so we went to a clinic in León to book an appointment. Luckily, we got a time slot for 10:00 a.m. the next morning, which felt both quick and reassuring. The rest of the morning was spent doing a bit of shopping to refresh our travel wardrobe, after 30 days on the road, a few items definitely needed replacing. At this point, you feel the wear not only on your body but on your clothes and gear too. In the afternoon, we had a meeting with sports journalist PA Gullö, who hosts the podcast Camino med PA. We met at a café right next to the cathedral in León, and recorded an episode. Unfortunately, the audio didn’t turn out well, so we had to re-record it a bit later. It was great to be part of podcast Camino med PA part 12, and we even got the chance to mention our Website! We wrapped up the day with a delicious pasta dinner at a cozy restaurant on the plaza in front of the cathedral. A busy and different kind of Camino day with no walking, but full of people, projects, and new experiences. That too, is part of the journey.

daysW5.title: León -> Villa de Mazarife
daysW5.short_desc: Back pain, taxi and booking mix-ups.
daysW5.long_desc: The day started with Roy visiting the naprapath we had booked in León due to continued back pain. After the treatment, he returned to the hotel to rest. The naprapath advised against walking that day, so we decided to take a taxi to our next planned stop, Villa de Mazarife. Since we’ve pre-booked our entire route, it’s difficult to make changes to the master plan. When we arrived at Hostal Tío Pepe, the owner couldn’t find our reservation, flipping through his handwritten notes in vain. After nearly an hour, he brought in a woman who was more familiar with the booking system. She quickly found our reservation and confirmed it was prepaid. What a relief! Unfortunately, our bag sent via Jackotrans never arrived. It had been left behind at the hotel in León and wouldn’t be delivered until the next day. So, we had to get through the evening with only what we had in our daypacks. Later, we ran into Lydia from California again. She looked exhausted, waiting for a ride to her accommodation, which was located on the alternate Camino route. Unfortunately, she had mistakenly followed the main trail, taking her off course. Dinner that evening was a rather mediocre pilgrim menu, but the company helped lift the mood, including a nice woman from Norway we shared the table with.

daysW5.title: Villa de Mazarife -> Hospital de Orbigio
daysW5.short_desc: A beautiful short walk to the Medieval Town of Hospital de Órbigo
daysW5.long_desc: After a much-needed rest day, today's 14 km walk to Hospital de Órbigo felt relaxed and enjoyable. With perfect weather, a manageable distance, and a comfortable pace, it turned out to be one of the more pleasant days on the Camino. As we approached the town, we immediately recognized the iconic stone bridge stretching across the river, a truly striking sight. Every year, this historic spot hosts medieval knight festivals, adding even more character and charm to the location. We stopped for a fresh salad lunch and shared a table with a father and daughter from New Zealand, also on their Camino journey. These kinds of encounters always bring joy and a sense of global connection. We then checked into Hotel Don Suero de Quiñones, which turned out to be a great choice  comfortable, welcoming, and offering a lovely view of the famous bridge. We ended the day with a tasty dinner at the hotel, the perfect close to a sunny, peaceful day on the trail.

daysW5.title: Hospital de Orbigio -> Astorga
daysW5.short_desc: Sheep on the trail, Gaudí architecture, and pasta in Astorga
daysW5.long_desc: We left Hospital de Órbigo on a beautiful morning, and not long into the walk we encountered a shepherd with a large flock of sheep and a few well-trained sheepdogs. The animals passed right next to us , a magical and very Camino moment that added charm to the start of the day. Much of today’s route felt familiar, as we had walked this stretch three years ago with a travel group led by Rolf´s Travel Agency. The memories came flooding back as we made our way toward the city of Astorga. Upon arrival, we checked in at the lovely Hotel Gaudí, right across from the city's iconic Palacio de Gaudi. Designed by the famous architect Antoni Gaudí and begun in 1899, the building now houses a museum, which we took the time to explore, both the architecture and exhibits were well worth the visit. We ended the day with a leisurely evening stroll through the charming streets of Astorga, followed by a pasta dinner at the hotel, served in a beautiful, traditionally decorated Spanish dining room. A perfect end to a day filled with history, scenery, and classic Camino encounters.
